newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria bank closures block industry.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria bank closures block industry.

text.p: Recent bank closures dealt a fresh blow to Bulgaria's stagnating industry by blocking the accounts of hundreds of state firms, Industry Minister Lyubomir Dachev said on Wednesday.

"There are many enterprises which are finding their way out of the crisis, but there are others that can do nothing and I am wondering how long the bank closures will last," Dachev told a news conference.

Bulgaria's central bank placed 14 troubled banks under special supervision in the past few months in an attempt to ascertain their financial state, decide which should seek solvency, and decide which should be stabilised.
The accounts of more than 300 state enterprises are blocked in one of the biggest local banks, the Economic Bank.
Some of these firms have accounts in other banks, others rely on latest revenue from sales but most can do nothing to avoid the crisis, said Dachev.
"The decision to block the banks was taken without consulting us and now it is difficult to estimate how much money from these industrial firms is blocked," he said.
He added it was impossible to borrow money at the current high interest rates without risking huge losses on repayments.
The central bank increased its central interest rate to a record 300 percent last month in a move to support the slumping lev and curb inflation.
"We discussed the problems with the central bank a few days ago and they promised to help resolve them shortly," said Dachev. He declined to elaborate.
Bulbank, Bulgaria's biggest commercial bank, is negotiating the takeover of Economic Bank, which would provide a partial solution.
The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank have pledged funds to support Bulgaria's tortuous transition on condition Sofia speeds up privatisation and closes loss-makers.
Shutting down a total of 64 loss-making enterprises is the short-term restructuring goal that Bulgaria has failed to meet so far but pledged to complete by end-October.

Of 38 enterprises earmarked for closure by the industry ministry, 17 have been restructured so far. Only 12 have been closed and a further five, among which are the Plama refinery and Pirin Plast plastics producer, have been sold off to local investors.
Most of the 18 agricultural loss-makers marked for liquidation will be sold to investors, agriculture minister Krastyo Trendafilov told the same news conference. -- Sofia Newsroom +359 2 84561
